GEOPHYSICS
A Newly Determined Paleomagnetic Pole for the Late Ordovician
in Siberia and Kinematics of the Siberian Platform
on the Time Interval of ~505–455 Ma Ago
V. E. Pavlova,*, A. M. Pasenkoa, A. V. Dronovb, and I. V. Fedyukina
Presented by Academician A.O. Gliko March 2, 2021
Received March 2, 2021; revised March 12, 2021; accepted March 12, 2021
Abstract—A paleomagnetic study of the Chertovskii Horizon of the Moyero River valley was carried out.
Based on published and newly obtained data, the sequence of seven reliable determinations of the paleomag-
netic pole position is obtained for Siberia within the time interval of ~505–450 Ma. This sequence makes it
possible to determine with high precision the paleogeographic position of the Siberian platform over a period
of ~50 Ma from the Middle Cambrian until the middle of the Upper Ordovician.
Keywords: Siberian Platform, Ordovician, Paleomagnetism, paleoreconstruction
DOI: 10.1134/S1028334X21060131

Fig. 1. Geographic and stratigraphic position of the studied section. (1) traps; (2) Silurian; (3) Upper Ordovician; (4) Middle
Ordovician; (5) Lower Ordovician; (6) Cambrian; (7) predominantly gray-colored strata of warm-water oolitic limestones with
stromatolites; (8) predominantly red-colored siltstones with crystal molds over halite and, sometimes, interlayers of gypsum;
(9)alternation of red-colored siltstones and gray-colored, mainly oolitic limestones; (10) the same with stromatolite interbeds in
the carbonate layers; (11) alternation of gray oolitic limestones with stromatolites and greenish gray siltstones with glauconite;
(12) alternation beds of gypsum and dolomite with stromatolite; (13) quartz sandstones; (14) limestones and clayey limestones
with Angarella bioherms; (15) violet and burgundy–red siltstones and fine-grained sandstones; (16) gray bioclastic limestones
and limestone conglomerates; (17) cold-water carbonates, alternation of greenish gray siltstones and bioclastic limestones. A cir-
cle with the number 70 indicates the location of the outcrop studied.

magnetometer manufactured by 2GEnterprise
(United States). In total, depending on the nature of
the paleomagnetic recording, from 12 to 18 cleaning
steps were performed up to temperatures correspond-
ing to the hematite Curie point (~670–680°C).
LABORATORY PALEOMAGNETIC STUDY
The values of the magnetic susceptibility and natu-
ral remanent magnetization (NRM) of the rocks stud-
ied varied from 40 to 250 × 10–6 SI units and from 1 ×
10–3 to 10–20 × 10–3 A/m, respectively.
